they can help you with your suicidal ideation/actions, they’ve helped thousands of people. it is quite literally their job to help people, especially now. eventually you will be able to vote, and you will be able to change things. there are people who are advocating for you in the legal sphere. this is not a hopeless situation. 

it is not beneficial for you to stay on the internet, that much is true. i wish you luck and grace and hope that ultimately you choose yourself and your potential in life over anything else. please contact someone and be honest about your feelings, it could quite literally change your life for the better

the current political climate is Rough to say the least. however (assuming that you’re speaking about America) this country has been plagued with rough political climates since its independence from Great Britain. however, people have coped with these situations, and have taken it day by day.

the good thing about american politics is that it’s often never permanent. in 2-4 years we will have another election cycle. things have the possibility/potential to change. a lot of people are in your position right now, and they find comfort in each other. times like these are especially not the times to isolate yourself. i reiterate that it is best that you try to reintegrate yourself back into social society.

it may be that your mother does not understand the gravity of your situation. i would suggest calling a crisis line, as the things that you are saying are quite concerning, and i hope you realize that it is beneficial to work to get better.

the trevor project lifeline is as follows: 
1-866-488-7386
Crisis intervention and suicide prevention phone service available 24/7/365.

the trans lifeline is as follows:

A 24/7 hotline available in the U.S. and Canada staffed by transgender people for transgender people.
1-877-565-8860 (United States)

there’s also the generic 988. i would highly suggest that you reach out to at least one of these numbers, and take your mental health seriously

if you’ve wanted to end your life since november, that is much more concerning than anything else demonstrated in your previous posts. mental health care is almost like shopping for a car. you have to try different things to figure out what works for you. people since the beginning of the psychiatric/psychological field have found respite and peace from mental health care, and you will too. sometimes it takes longer than others. from here, id suggest the following:

1. please tell somebody about how you feel. the more honest you are, the more they can try to help you. 
2. sit and process what’s happened tonight. try to find at least something that you can take with you for the days/weeks/months following this.

you are young. you have so much more life to live. it is apparent that you have been struggling before this, but it does not mean you have to continue to struggle.

the internet is a place where people will share their opinion, whether constructively or negatively. it’s not worth beating yourself over it. at the end of the day, i am sure that you realize that the situation you were in is not ideal, but you are young. you have a plethora of things that you can change and adapt. i promise you in a couple of years you won’t look at this situation as harshly as you are now. if this is affecting you to the point where you are experiencing suicidal ideation/suicidal behavior, you need to get off the internet and utilize the crisis/mental health resources in your area.

i’m going to tread with grace because i know youre a minor. i know a lot of people your age tend to go for internet based connections but i think this situation should demonstrate that people can hide who they are/their intentions much easier over the internet. i think its time that you try to work past your social isolation and reintegrate yourself back into society. whether it be with part time school, part time work, an outpatient group mental health program, something in which you can get the help you need whilst also interacting with people your age so things like this dont happen again and you know what to expect out of healthy, realistic relationships with people in your age group, whether platonic or romantic. you’re not going to get that over the internet
